precepts.text: The land was not to be sold forever, for it belonged to the Most High and was held as a family inheritance.
precepts.point: Naboth refused because the land was the inheritance of his fathers. He could not simply hand off an inheritance that was given to him.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
“The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me.” The land belonged to the Most High and was held as a family inheritance.

Ahab wanted Naboth’s vineyard in Jezreel because it was hard by his palace, and offered a better vineyard or “the worth of it in money.” But Naboth answered, “The Lord forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.” He could not simply hand off an inheritance that was given to him. He was keeping the law.

precepts.text: A king sealed the den with his own signet so the decree could not be changed, showing the binding authority of a royal seal.
precepts.point: She commanded them to proclaim a fast, set Naboth on high, and set two sons of Belial before him to bear false witness that he blasphemed God and the king, then stone him. This was evil counsel and a murderous plot.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
“And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.” A king sealed the den with his own signet so the decree could not be changed. That is the binding authority of a royal seal.

Jezebel “wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them with his seal”. The seal was a signet, the official mark of the king’s authority, so when those letters reached the elders and nobles of Naboth’s city, they carried royal weight as if Ahab himself had written them.

precepts.text: The commandment forbids bearing false witness, which is exactly what the sons of Belial were hired to do.
precepts.point: She commanded them to proclaim a fast, set Naboth on high, and set two sons of Belial before him to bear false witness that he blasphemed God and the king, then stone him. This was evil counsel and a murderous plot.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.”

That is exactly what the sons of Belial were hired to do. Jezebel wrote, “set two men, sons of Belial, before him, to bear witness against him, saying, Thou didst blaspheme God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him, that he may die.” A fast proclaimed, Naboth set on high, and false witnesses brought in to kill him. It was evil counsel and a murderous plot, built on breaking the commandment.

precepts.text: The Most High condemns those who greedily gain of their neighbors by extortion and shed blood, smiting his hand against dishonest gain.
precepts.point: Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
“In thee have they taken gifts to shed blood; thou hast taken usury and increase, and thou hast greedily gained of thy neighbours by extortion, and hast forgotten me, saith the Lord God. Behold, therefore I have smitten mine hand at thy dishonest gain which thou hast made, and at thy blood which hath been in the midst of thee.”

When Naboth was dead, Jezebel said, “Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give thee for money”, and Ahab rose up to go down and take it. That is extortion: seizing what another has by violence and force, and greedily gaining of a neighbour with blood.

Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward. The Most High smites his hand at that dishonest gain.

precepts.text: The same judgment was spoken over Jeroboam, cutting off every male and taking away the remnant of his house like dung.
precepts.point: The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
The same judgment was spoken over Jeroboam: “Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.”

The words “him that pisseth against the wall” mean the males. The Most High said he would cut them off entirely. Now Elijah speaks the same words over Ahab, because he “sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord”: every male cut off, and his house made “like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat”, for the provocation by which he made Israel to sin.

precepts.text: When Zimri reigned he slew all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male among his kinsfolk or friends.
precepts.point: The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
This is how the judgment on Baasha was carried out: “when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.” When Zimri reigned, not one male was left.

So when the Most High tells Ahab, “And will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah”, it is plain what that means. The house of Baasha was wiped out to the last male, and the same was coming on Ahab’s house for the provocation wherewith he provoked the Most High and made Israel to sin.

precepts.text: A curse of disobedience is that the carcass becomes meat for the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth, with none to fray them away.
precepts.point: Any of Ahab's house dying in the city the dogs would eat, and any dying in the field the fowls of the air would eat, matching the curses spoken in the law.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
“And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.” That is one of the curses of disobedience in the law.

The Most High declared, “The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Him that dieth of Ahab in the city the dogs shall eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat.” The judgment on Ahab’s house matches the curse spoken in the law: their carcases left as meat for the beasts and the birds.
